source: Review round 2, R2C-25 and R2C-26 (saas-app-change-cost.md); RFC 0007 §7.4.3, §7.5
statement: A grant analysis makes at most its comparison budget of comparisons, spent in the analysis's order, and over it never answers contained: a statement still being compared when the budget runs out is granted, and every fragment it reaches past the budget is unknown (too large to analyze), so what it did not compare needs approval. It splits a change into at most its fragment bound (80,000: what the budget checks at the largest legitimate change's 50 comparisons a fragment), counting each statement's actions times resources before splitting it: a change that grants more is too large to analyze, nothing of it is split or decided, and it is one escalation; the fragments past the comparison budget are one escalation too, never one each (DR1-E-1).
guards: control:ComparisonBudgetTest#past the budget a fragment is too large to analyze, never contained
control:ComparisonBudgetTest#a statement still being compared when the budget runs out is granted
control:ComparisonBudgetTest#the same change stops at the same comparison
control:ComparisonBudgetTest#a change that splits into more fragments than one analysis splits is too large, and nothing is split
control:ComparisonBudgetTest#the fragments up to the bound are split and analysed, one more is too large
control:UnknownEscalationsTest#a change too large to split is one escalation
control:UnknownEscalationsTest#every fragment past the comparison budget is one escalation, counted
